To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) the optimization objective of the original GAN is not consistent, and the original GAN does not converge to a global optimum; 2) the optimization objective in WGAN is consistent, and WGAN does converge to a global optimal; 3) WGAN is stable and can produce meaningful learning curves; 4) the optimal of WGAN corresponds to a Wasserstein distance; 5) WGAN is equivalent to adversarial training of energy-based models.

1) we introduce WGANs, a new algorithm for training generative models, 2) we provide theoretical justifications for WGANs, and 3) we show that WGANs lead to state-of-the-art results on different image datasets.
we introduce WGAN, a new GAN model, that is more stable and easier to train and debug, and that is theoretically well founded.
